title: CIDER: A Dataset of Contextual Disclosure Boundaries for Privacy Preference Alignment
abstract: arXiv:2608.09164v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Aligning large language models (LLMs) with human privacy preferences requires capturing individuals' disclosure boundaries beyond general privacy norms. However, a gap remains in eliciting such nuanced preferences to evaluate alignment in realistic settings. We introduce CIDER, a dataset of 14,850 human annotations from 169 users, forming 1,650 contextual disclosure boundary sets across 60 interpersonal communication scenarios involving information sharing that violates privacy norms. Each boundary represents a real user's disclosure decisions over 9 sharing variants in a scenario, for a given communication role and AI-mediated condition. We formulate a task in which models predict a user's disclosure decision from historical boundaries, with varying levels of contextual information. Across 12 open and proprietary models, in-context personalization improves prediction accuracy by up to 11.41 percentage points using only 6 historical

translated_title: CIDER：用于隐私偏好对齐的上下文披露边界数据集
translated_abstract: 摘要：使大型语言模型（LLMs）与人类隐私偏好对齐，需要捕捉个体在一般隐私规范之外的披露边界。然而，在现实场景中，如何引出这些细微的偏好以评估对齐效果仍存在空白。我们引入了CIDER，这是一个包含来自169位用户的14,850条人工注释的数据集，形成了60个人际沟通场景中的1,650组上下文披露边界集，这些场景涉及违反隐私规范的信息共享。每个边界代表一个真实用户在一个场景中，针对给定的沟通角色和AI中介条件，对9种共享变体的披露决策。我们设定了一个任务，即模型从历史边界中预测用户的披露决策，并提供不同级别的上下文信息。在12个开放和专有模型中，仅使用6条历史记录进行上下文个性化，预测准确率最多可提高11.41个百分点。
tldr: 本文提出了CIDER数据集，通过捕捉个体在人际沟通中的上下文披露边界，显著提升了LLM在隐私偏好对齐中的个性化预测能力。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces CIDER, a dataset capturing contextual disclosure boundaries in interpersonal communication, which significantly improves LLM personalized prediction for privacy preference alignment.
